page: The UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 12 physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core performance for this configuration. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieved a score of 3942.28, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression at 42.79 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 19.58 GB/sec also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 45719.52 and a PassMark CPU score of 35206.69, both falling within the average range. For language model tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens/sec using a small 135M model, while prompt processing for the same model operates at an average speed of 1842.33 tokens/sec.

This server offers a specialized hardware profile that balances dual-GPU acceleration with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Because local storage is absent, workloads must rely on network-attached storage solutions. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for sustained multi-core CPU-bound tasks, though the top-tier single-core performance and dedicated GPU hardware mitigate this for targeted applications. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for GPU-driven workloads that require substantial VRAM and system memory without requiring massive multi-core CPU scaling. It is suitable for machine learning inference, small-scale LLM text generation, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering or simulation tasks.
description: The UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a KVM-based, GPU-accelerated server designed for memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor offering 12 shared vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 128.0 GB of system memory, and dual NVIDIA L4 Ada Lovelace GPUs with a total of 48 GB VRAM. No local storage is included. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the top 10%. Additionally, it delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens/sec for small LLM models. Multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth metrics remain in the average tier. This server is well-suited for machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and data science workloads that leverage dual-GPU acceleration and high system memory density.
